newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Muhammad Ali back in Africa, still the greatest.
newsitem.headline: Muhammad Ali back in Africa, still the greatest.

text.p: Muhammad Ali, trembling from Parkinson's disease but still sparring, made an emotional return to Africa on Tuesday, stopping in Ivory Coast to deliver aid to refugee children from Liberia.
Even military guards joined in the chant of "Ali, akwaba!" (Welcome, Ali) as the 55-year-old heavyweight boxing legend arrived at a packed news conference at the sports ministry in Abidjan.
With a glint in his eye, Ali listened attentively as a translator whispered into his ear, a grin playing across his lips when the minister called him "the greatest".
Barely audible, he told officials to "find your best heavywight and I'll do two rounds with him before I go".
He rose to swap fake punches with African heavyweight champion Augustin N'gou, and with two lighter ex-champions from an earlier age, one with tears in his eyes.

Ali took pains to say that his main aim in life was to spread the word of Islam, but his minders refocused attention back on the humanitarian reason for his visit, and on a company donating a "revolutionary new soy-based meat substitute" to Liberian refugees.

But the journalists, soldiers and ministry workers were more interested in past glories, a loud cheer rising at the mention of "Zaire, 1974". The reference was to Ali's finest hour, the "Rumble in the Jungle" when he defeated fellow American George Foreman to reclaim the world title.
Ali sported a black shirt bearing the name of his charity, "Global Village Champions", which is behind the humanitarian mission.

He was moved by a plea from Sister Sponsa Beltran, whose orphanage for handicapped Liberian children was forced to move over the border to the port town of San Pedro in Ivory Coast in 1994 at the height of Liberia's seven-year civil war.
Ali's programme includes a visit to San Pedro on Wednesday to deliver food and wheelchairs to the children.
